Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Document-level:

- Scheme: A

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V.
- Person responsible: C. Oosterman
- Title: Head Certification Board
- Phone: +31 78 6332332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl

- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Applicants:
- Mettler-Toledo (Changzhou) Precision Instruments Ltd., No. 22, Zhengqiang Road, XinBei District, Changzhou, Jiangsu 213125, Peoples Republic of China

Manufacturers: same as applicant (label says "Applicant and Manufacturer"). Should I add it? The label says "Applicant and Manufacturer" so I'll add the same entity as a manufacturer too.

Certified type:
- Category: Load cell
- Type designations: MT1241 (the "MT1241....." — dots may be masking? Probably "MT1241". I'll use "MT1241". Actually the markdown shows "MT1241....." — could be trailing dots from redaction or just part of OCR. I'll use "MT1241".)
- Module designation: Analog load cell (single point load cell with strain gauges — an analog load cell). Hmm, "single point load cell, with strain gauges" — module designation for R60 would be "Analog load cell" or "Digital load cell". Given the characteristics (rated output in mV/V, input/output impedance), it's analog. I'll set "Analog load cell".
- Description: "A single point load cell, with strain gauges."

Model family: Emax range "30 kg up to and including 250 kg" — this is a range, not discrete models. So no model family. Type-level characteristics.

Characteristics (type_level):
- maximum_capacity: {min: 30, max: 250}, unit kg
- minimum_dead_load: 0, kg
- accuracy_class: "C"
- rated_output: 2.0 with tolerance ±0.2 mV/V. Hmm. Value could be {nominal...} but schema says value is number | {min,max} | string. I could do value: 2, unit mV/V, and maybe a separate attribute rated_output_tolerance. Or value string "2.0 ± 0.2". Better: rated_output: value 2, unit_symbol "mV/V", plus rated_output_tolerance: 0.2 mV/V. Convert decimal comma: 2,0 → 2.0 → 2; 0,2 → 0.2.
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 3500, footnote marker 1)
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 10000, footnote marker 1)
- ratio_z_emax_over_2dr: 3500, footnote 1) — label "ratio_z_emax_over_dr"? The formula is Z = Emax / (2 * DR). Canonical: ratio_z_emax_over_2dr.
- input_impedance: 410 Ω ± 10 Ω → value 410, unit "Ω", plus input_impedance_tolerance 10. Or value string. I'll do impedance with tolerance separate attributes. Alternatively value: {min: 400, max: 420}. Hmm, ± tolerance could be a range: 400–420 Ω. That's arguably accurate. I'll represent input_impedance: {min:400, max:420} unit Ω? That loses the nominal. I think best: input_impedance: value 410, unit_symbol "Ω", and input_impedance_tolerance: value 10, unit_symbol "Ω". Similar for output impedance 350 ± 4.
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, °C
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- recommended_excitation_voltage: {min:5, max:15}, V, power_supply_type "AC / DC"? The excitation "5 - 15 V AC / DC" → voltage 5–15 V, excitation_type "AC/DC". I'll add recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC".
- excitation_maximum: 20 V AC/DC → excitation_max_voltage: 20, V, type AC/DC. Maybe just one type attribute "AC / DC" covering both. I'll add excitation_type: "AC/DC".
- transducer_material: "Aluminium alloy"
- atmospheric_protection: "Silicon rubber"

Footnotes: Remarks item 1: "The characteristics for nmax, Y and Z can be reduced separately." That's a remark, but it's referenced via (1) markers on n, Y, Z. So footnote marker "1)" with that text.

Test reports:
- R60/2000-NL1-06.04A, 2003-05-09, 37 pages, role: test_report (OIML Test Report)
- R60/2000-NL1-06.04B, 2003-05-09, 38 pages, test_report
- NMi-1902131-01, 2018-12-20, 26 pages, test_report
- NMi-1902131-02, 2018-12-20, 24 pages, test_report

Recommendation: R60, edition 2000, amendment null, accuracy_classes ["C"], scheme A.

Revision history: not present. Omit.

Matrix tables: none.

Date issued: 20 December 2018 → "2018-12-20".

certificate.page_total: 2.

Now output JSON. No model_family since range, not discrete models. Actually could one argue a family of load cells 30–250 kg? The rule says include model_family only if cert covers >1 model variant with discrete values. The range "30 kg up to and including 250 kg" — it's a range of capacities for the single type MT1241. I'll keep type_level with range value.

Let me write the JSON.

For rated output, using value as string "2.0 ± 0.2" would violate numeric preference... Rule: values MUST be objects with numeric value. I'll split: rated_output (2, mV/V) and rated_output_tolerance (0.2, mV/V). Similarly input_impedance 410 Ω + input_impedance_tolerance 10 Ω; output_impedance 350 Ω + output_impedance_tolerance 4 Ω.

Footnote markers: "1)".

Edition: "Edition 2000 (E)" → int 2000.

Should footnote_markers be omitted when empty? Omit to keep clean. Include footnote_markers only where referenced: n, Y, Z get ["1)"].

Safe overload: value 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: {"value": "Emax", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}. Hmm the structured form requires unit_symbol and unit_id keys? "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape". I'll include unit_symbol and unit_id as null for string values. Keep consistent.

Recommended excitation: 5–15 V, AC/DC. Add recommended_excitation_type: {"value": "AC/DC", ...}. And excitation_type for maximum? Excitation maximum 20 V AC/DC. I'll have excitation_maximum_voltage: 20 V, and excitation_type: "AC / DC" — a single type attribute covering both. To be safe: recommended_excitation_voltage (5–15 V), recommended_excitation_type ("AC/DC"), excitation_maximum (20 V), excitation_maximum_type ("AC/DC"). That's a bit redundant; I'll use excitation_current_type? Keep simple: recommended_excitation_voltage, recommended_excitation_type, excitation_maximum_voltage, excitation_maximum_type.

n attribute label: "max_load_cell_intervals_nlc" per rules example ("Max. number of load cell intervals nLC"). Good.

Y: "ratio_y_emax_over_vmin". Z: "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr".

Temperature: {"value": {"min": -10, "max": 40}, "unit_symbol": "°C"}.

Project number: keep as string "1902131".

Write final JSON without fences.
